Let’s not lose sight of what this really is: a glaring symptom of a rigged economic system that always protects property owners and landlords while trampling on the human right to shelter. 

While working-class families and vulnerable people bear the brunt of the landlord class's backlash, the political establishment just spins the numbers to protect the status quo. We saw this firsthand in Limerick this past week when Taoiseach Micheál Martin had the absolute nerve to boast that housing tenancies have increased, completely glossing over the devastating human cost of his own administration's policies. 

Sure, the Government pats itself on the back for introducing new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants, but it's completely half-hearted. It leaves gaping loopholes that landlords can weaponize against tenants to protect their profit margins. 

The reality on the ground—which the establishment actively tries to sweep under the rug—is a shameful rise in eviction notices and homelessness, with the numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increasing again. Instead of confronting the deep structural inequality driving this housing crisis, they are just pushing the most vulnerable people right out onto the streets.
